contents.direction_remark: Continues a block from the previous page (f. 78v), this is its tail; line 2 ends at the left with 'wa-huwa' + an Arabic word. Signs are Latin-letter-like (T, A, H, U, C shapes), a different alphabet from the curved hooked signs of the block below. Counts approximate.

contents.text: وهو فد[ي?]م / فبتّ أكتّم عينيها ومن عجب إني أقبّل أسيافا فأسفك دمي / ومن ذلك الذي حلّه مرتين
contents.note: line 2 left end 'wa-huwa' then one word not read with certainty ('fdym'/'qdym'?); line 3 = verse 'so I spent the night concealing her two eyes; and strangely I kiss swords and shed my blood'; line 4 = introductory phrase 'and of that, the one he solved twice'

contents.direction_remark: Hooked/curved signs, lam-alif-like pairs frequent, small boxes and triangles as rare signs. Dividers = dotted vertical stroke, about 3 per line. Counts approximate.

contents.text: وكنت متى أرسلت طرفك رائدا لقلبك يوما أتعبتك المناظر / رأيت الذي لا كله أنت قادر عليه ولا عن بعضه أنت صابر
contents.note: verse, answers block lines 5-10 presumably (no explicit 'halaltuhu' on this page)

contents.text: ومن ذلك من خمس خمسة من أبيات إلى إسحق الصابي
contents.note: read with doubt for 'min khams khamsa min abyat'; 'ila Ishaq al-Sabi' clear. Continues on next page.

correspondents.note: named in line 13 as the poet/addressee of the following five-verse item; no formula after the name on this page (rahimahu Allah not seen)

technique_remarks: fa-halaltuhu formula not seen on this page; 'حلّه مرتين' = 'he solved it twice' (line 4)
plaintext_for: lines 1-2 cipher: its plaintext is the verse in line 3 (block began on previous page f. 78v); lines 5-10 cipher: verse in lines 11-12
certainty: medium: clean page, no worm damage; sign counts approximate; one word in line 2 and the phrase in line 13 uncertain. No dates, no AH years.

contents.direction_remark: Block follows the heading 'to Ishaq al-Sabi' on f. 79r line 13 (so likely the five-verse item). Hebrew/square-letter-like signs (K, N, n, 7, 3 shapes) plus hooked ones; dividers ~4 per line. Line 5 ends at the left with 'wa-huwa'. Counts approximate.

contents.text: وهو / أرى دهري على ضعفي تعدّى وجاوز حدّ تهذيبي وعدّ[ى?] / وصيّرني له غرضا معدّا / وأيام تعدّ عليّ عتبا وحظي من رغائبها يفوت
contents.note: 'and it is:' then verses: 'I see my fate has overstepped against my weakness and exceeded the limit of my correction...; and made me a target prepared for it; and days count blame against me while my share of their desirables slips away'. Last word of line 6 uncertain.

contents.text: ومن ذلك منها
contents.note: 'and of that, from them' (introduces next cipher)

contents.direction_remark: Different sign set: curved Arabic-cursive-like signs (sin-like, ayn-like hooks, small circles). Block runs to the bottom of the page and continues overleaf (f. 80r). Counts approximate.

correspondents.note: no new name on this page

technique_remarks: 'ومن ذلك منها' = 'and of that, of them' (no technique stated)
plaintext_for: first block (lines 1-5): plaintext verses lines 6-8 on this page; second block (lines 10-13): continues on next page f. 80r
certainty: medium: no worm damage, signs clear; counts approximate, one word in line 6 uncertain. No dates, no rahimahu Allah formula.

contents.direction_remark: Tail of the curved/cursive-sign block that began at the bottom of f. 79v (lines 10-13). Last line of the block; 'wa-huwa' on line 2. Counts approximate.

contents.text: وهو / كمالي بما ينقص [ثمين?] وعلمي كلّه درّ ثمين / وعند[ي?] سرّها ودّي مبين / مكاني من خصيصته مكين وحالي من خصاصتها [تنوف?]
contents.note: line 2 'and it is:'; then verse lines. Several words uncertain (difficult hand with heavy vowelling); not paraphrased.

contents.text: وممّا كتبته له أسبغ الله ظلاله ما كان [ترجم/نرجم?] لي من نظمه الشيخ / شمس الدين خطيب الصالحية بدمشق المحروسة بقلم آخر / يورّي فيها بسبعة أقلام
contents.note: 'and of what I wrote to him, may God extend his shadow, what was [?] for me of the verse of the shaykh Shams al-Din, preacher (khatib) of al-Salihiyya in Damascus the guarded, in another pen (hand/script), concealing in it with seven pens (scripts)'. The words after 'ma kana' are not read with certainty.

contents.direction_remark: Curved cursive-like signs with loops, tiny dotted circles and 'bowl' shapes; first block of the 'seven pens' item, one of seven scripts. No red letters. A paper crack/repair thread crosses lines 10-12 on the right. Block continues overleaf (f. 80v). Counts approximate.

correspondents.arabic: الشيخ شمس الدين خطيب الصالحية بدمشق المحروسة
correspondents.translit: al-Shaykh Shams al-Din, khatib of al-Salihiyya in Damascus the guarded
correspondents.note: no patronymic written out; the formula after him is on the preceding phrase: 'asbagha Allah zilalahu' (may God extend his shadow), i.e. the compiler writes of him as ALIVE. Note the formula follows 'ma kataba-hu lahu' ('what I wrote to him'), so it refers to Shams al-Din as addressee.

technique_remarks: يورّي فيها بسبعة أقلام = 'concealing in it with seven pens (seven scripts)': a multi-script cipher in several hands/alphabets, by Shams al-Din (or the compiler; reading of the subject uncertain)
بقلم آخر = 'in another pen/script'
plaintext_for: first (curved sign) block on lines 1: continues f. 79v lines 10-13, plaintext = verse lines 3-5 on this page. Second block lines 9-13: no plaintext on this page; continues f. 80v
certainty: medium: clear page; sign counts approximate; several words of the verses and the heading uncertain. No year given. Key dating evidence: asbagha Allah zilalahu after Shams al-Din's mention (alive).

contents.text: فحلها سريعا وأرسلها ولما أبدها لجوابه وترجمته / مذكورة في كتاب الأجوبة الشامية
contents.note: 'so he solved it quickly and sent it ..., and its translation is mentioned in the Book of the Syrian (Damascene) Answers (Kitab al-Ajwiba al-Shamiyya)'. This answers the 'seven pens' block on f. 80r lines 9-13; the compiler gives no plaintext here but refers to another book. Middle words of line 1 uncertain.

contents.text: ومن / غبار ذُوبِ الرفاع بحفوف بنسخ كرام كانين عدول [?] / وتوفيع ريحاني رجائي لعفو من ناديك ثلث الليل عند نزول [?]
contents.note: verse fragments (poetic), reading very uncertain; 'ومن' at left end of line 2 begins an item. Not paraphrased.

contents.text: ثم كتبت له ما ترجمه لي الشيخ ناصر الدين [بن؟] سلار بدمشق أيضا / لما رأى حلّ هذا المذكور وجوابه مع قصيدة مذكورة في / الأجوبة الشامية وجوابها وورّى فيه بخمسة عشر / نوعا من الكتابة في أربعة أبيات منها
contents.note: 'then I wrote to him what al-Shaykh Nasir al-Din [ibn?] Sallar translated/rendered for me in Damascus also, when he saw the solution of this (item) mentioned and its answer with a qasida mentioned in the Shami Answers and its reply, and he concealed in it fifteen kinds of writing in four verses; of them:'. The name reads 'Nasir al-Din Sallar' (possibly with 'ibn'); no patronymic written beyond that.

contents.direction_remark: Same curved/cursive-sign family as f. 80r with small loops and bowl shapes; a thin crack/repair thread crosses the left end of lines 11-13. This is the first of the 'fifteen kinds of writing in four verses'. No red letters. Counts approximate.

correspondents.translit: al-Shaykh Nasir al-Din (ibn?) Sallar, in Damascus
correspondents.note: no formula (no rahimahu Allah / ayyadahu Allah) after the name on this page; he is said to have 'translated/rendered' the item for the compiler

technique_remarks: ووريّ فيه بخمسة عشر نوعا من الكتابة = 'he veiled in it with fifteen kinds of writing'
في أربعة أبيات = 'in four verses'
كتاب الأجوبة الشامية = cited work: Book of the Syrian (Damascene) Answers
plaintext_for: lines 1-2 refer to the block on f. 80r (lines 9-13); the block on this page (lines 9-13) has no plaintext on this page
certainty: medium: clean page; name Sallar and verse fragments uncertain; counts approximate. No dates; no AH year.

contents.text: فحلّه في أسرع وقت وأرسله وهو / نسخ ريحان عارضيك نسيب بحواشي رقاع حسنك ملحق / ثلث عمر العذول فيك يقضى في غبار [?] فلبّي وصلي بحقوق [?]
contents.note: 'so he solved it in the quickest time and sent it, and it is:' + verse lines; verse words (esp. lines 2-3) uncertain, not paraphrased. Answers the block of f. 80v lines 9-13 (the first of the 'fifteen kinds of writing in four verses').

contents.text: فكتبت تمامه وغيّرت الحروف
contents.note: 'so I wrote its completion (the remainder) and changed the letters'; a small mark (a single small letter, looks like ح or ط) sits just below the line in the middle.

contents.direction_remark: Same family of curved cursive-like signs (bowls, loops, small dotted circles) as ff. 80r-80v, but 'letters changed' (a different alphabet, per line 4). Counts approximate; last line short.

contents.text: فحلّه [سريعا?/ربيعا?] وأرسله وهو / إن تكن قاتلي بطول ما هجر وشعر العذار قلبي معلّق / فلقد باح سلوتي عنك توقيع غدا مزوّجا وذلك أوثق [?]
contents.note: 'so he solved it [quickly?] and sent it, and it is:' + verse: 'if you are my killer by the length of your shunning, and the down on your cheek (the hair of the beard-line) has my heart suspended...'. Third line very uncertain. A crack/repair thread crosses the right end of lines 12-13.

contents.text: زهر ٩ (?)
contents.note: catchword at foot of page, left of centre: reads like 'zahr' + a numeral-like mark; uncertain

technique_remarks: وغيّرت الحروف = 'and I changed the letters' (a new alphabet/substitution for the second cipher)
فكتبت تمامه = 'I wrote its completion' (full text of the item)
plaintext_for: lines 1-3: answer to the block on previous page f. 80v lines 9-13; lines 11-13: answer to the block on this page lines 5-10
certainty: medium: no names, no dates. Verses partly uncertain; counts approximate.

contents.text: ولما رأيته قد تمرّن في هذا الأمر ولم يصعب عليه صعب / ولم تعسر عليه عسر انتقيت له بيتين من نظم ابن الرومي / غريبة الألفاظ كثيرة الضادات فقليلة الألفات [?] / عويصة وظننتها يعسر حلها وربما تقعد في حلها أيام / لأن فيها [لغة/لعنة؟] فقلة الاستعمال للّام وترجمتها
contents.note: 'and when I saw that he had become practised in this matter, and nothing hard was hard for him and nothing difficult difficult, I chose for him two verses from the verse of Ibn al-Rumi, strange in words, many dads, few alifs, abstruse, and I thought its solving would be hard and days might pass over it, because in it is [a strange word?/curse?], the rarity of the use of lam, and its rendering (translation):'. Line 3-5 words uncertain.

contents.direction_remark: Different sign set again: digit-like signs (7, 8, 5, 6, 4 shapes), small angular hooks and one vertical-bar-with-hook sign that recurs at line ends (looks like a very frequent letter). Dividers ~4 per line. Counts approximate.

contents.text: فحلّه سريعا فيا لله العجب أشهد بالله أنه لو كتب هذا المنجّم [لجماعة؟] / من أصحاب التصانيف المقدّم ذكرهم لعجزوا عنه فسبحان / الوهاب ومن أي باب يدخل الإنسان إلى هذا المنجم
contents.note: comment, not the plaintext verses: 'so he solved it quickly - by God, the wonder! I swear by God that if this had been written for a group of authors of compilations mentioned before, they would have failed at it; glory to the Giver (al-Wahhab); and by what door does a person enter this mine/this astrologer (al-munajjim)?'. 'al-munajjim' is read as written (astrologer / or 'mine'), sense uncertain.

contents.text: وهو
contents.note: catchword at foot of page, left

correspondents.note: poet (d. 283 AH, 896 AD), named only as the source of the two verses; no formula (rahimahu Allah) after him on this page. The solver is not named; he is called 'al-munajjim' (the astrologer) possibly.

technique_remarks: بيتين من نظم ابن الرومي غريبة الألفاظ كثيرة الضادات = 'two verses of Ibn al-Rumi, strange words, many dads' (chosen as a hard text)
فقلة الاستعمال للّام = 'rarity of use of lam' (hard because of the letter distribution; reading uncertain)
plaintext_for: block lines 6-10: plaintext verses follow on next page (catchword 'wa-huwa'); lines 11-13 are a remark about the solver's speed
certainty: medium: clean page with a crack along the left edge of lines 11-13; some words uncertain. No dates.

contents.text: ضرب في الضريب أم أغريض وابتسام أم درّ ثغر ومبض / ضعفت مني وأمرض جسمي ودوا[ي] طرف ضعيف مريض
contents.note: the two Ibn al-Rumi verses (plaintext to the block on f. 81v lines 6-10), reading approximate: 'is it honey (darb) in frozen milk/ice (darib), or palm-spathe (ighrid), and a smile or pearls of a mouth and ...; my strength weakened, my body sick, my medicine a weak sick glance'. Several words uncertain, esp. the end of line 1.

contents.text: الضرب العسل الأبيض والضريب الجليد الذي جمد / في الشتاء في الأرض الباردة في اللبك [?] والأغريض الطلع
contents.note: lexical gloss on the rare words: 'al-darb is white honey, al-darib is the ice that froze in winter in the cold land...; al-ighrid is the palm-spathe (tal')'. The word 'اللبك' is uncertain.

contents.text: ولمّا أردت إرسال المواقيع الشريفة إلى الشام وكان / لي وصول من بيت المال بدمشق المحروسة مجري على / عن جملة ولم يحصل منه شيء فقصدت مثالا شريفا / إلى نائب غزة بخلاص الوصول [بحجة؟] المواقيع والأمثلة فكتبت
contents.note: 'and when I wished to send the noble decrees/signatures (al-mawaqi' al-sharifa) to Syria, and I had a receipt from the Treasury (bayt al-mal) in Damascus the guarded, charged against ... for a sum, and nothing was obtained from it, I sought a noble order (mithal) to the deputy (na'ib) of Gaza for the settlement of the receipt [on the strength of?] the decrees and the orders; so I wrote'. 'فكتبت' stands alone in the left margin at the level of lines 7-8 (end of line 8 displaced). Lines 6-8 uncertain in several words; 'مثالا شريفا' could be 'مثال الأشرف' (al-Ashraf?) - not certain.

contents.direction_remark: A new sign set: angular/straight signs ('=' bars, triangles, tridents, cup-and-bar shapes, small hooks), dotted dividers 5 per line. Line 12 begins with an Arabic-looking 'و' joined to the first sign. A paper crack/repair crosses the right of lines 11-13. This is the cipher letter 'I wrote' to the na'ib of Gaza (no plaintext on this page). Counts approximate.

correspondents.note: office only, no personal name, no patronymic, no formula (no rahimahu/ayyadahu) after it

technique_remarks: none on this page; the cipher is used for a real administrative letter (decrees, Treasury receipt, Damascus, Gaza)
plaintext_for: lines 1-2 are the plaintext verses for the block on previous page f. 81v lines 6-10; block lines 9-13 has plaintext presumably overleaf f. 82v
certainty: medium: names no persons; the dating hint is only institutional (Treasury of Damascus, na'ib of Gaza, possibly 'al-Ashraf' - not certain). No AH year on the page.

contents.direction_remark: Tail (last line) of the angular-sign block from f. 82r lines 9-13, for the na'ib of Gaza; solved immediately after on line 2. Counts approximate.

contents.text: فحلّه في الحال لسهولته وهو / يا سيدي فذا حالنا على غزة وما حصل من وصولي لا ولا [رزء؟] / نحتاج من جاهك العالي إلى همّة عسى يجيء ما يوصلني إلى غزة
contents.note: 'so he solved it at once because of its ease, and it is:' then the letter: 'O my lord, this is our state concerning Gaza, and nothing came of my arrival [receipt?]...; we need from your exalted standing a resolve, perhaps what will bring me to Gaza (comes)'. Several words uncertain ('غنّ' read as غزة). Answers the block on f. 82r lines 9-13 (and this page line 1).

contents.text: وممّا كتبه لي أمين الدين قاضي حماه فحللته بحضوره [?] / وأرسلته إلى المخدوم المشار [إليه] بعد ذلك فحلّه هذا البيت
contents.note: 'and of what Amin al-Din, qadi of Hama, wrote to me; and I solved it [in his presence?] and sent it to the master referred to (al-makhdum al-mushar ilayhi) afterwards, and he solved it, this verse'. The word 'اليه' (ilayhi) stands detached in the left margin at the end of line 6 together with a small sign. 'بحضوره' uncertain.

contents.direction_remark: Short block; signs digit-like or Arabic-letter-like ('ع', 'م', 'ك', 'لا', 7, 5 shapes) with wide spacing, a three-bar sign in line 9; dividers few. Last line short. Counts approximate.

contents.text: أصبحت أشهر شكري من رضاكم وأضمر الودّ فكم [رأى؟]
contents.note: verse, presumably the plaintext for the 4-line block above (lines 7-10); last word uncertain

contents.text: وممّا كتبه لي أيضا في مدح لكمال القاضي أمين الدين المذكور [اضمارا؟] [رد؟] / وجعل فواصله حرفا من جنس الأشكال
contents.note: 'and of what he also wrote to me in praise of (?) Kamal the qadi Amin al-Din the aforementioned; and he made its dividers (fawasil) a letter of the kind of the shapes (signs)'. A small word 'اضمارا' sits above line 12; the end of line 12 (after 'المذكور') is cut by a crack and uncertain.

correspondents.note: also 'al-qadi Amin al-Din al-madhkur' (the aforementioned) and 'Kamal [?] al-qadi Amin al-Din'; no patronymic; no formula (rahimahu/ayyadahu) after the name on this page; 'wa-mimma kataba li' ('of what he wrote to me') suggests he is the correspondent (living, but not stated)

correspondents.translit: al-makhdum al-mushar ilayhi (the master referred to)
correspondents.note: unnamed; he solved the cipher sent to him

technique_remarks: وجعل فواصله حرفا من جنس الأشكال = 'and he made its dividers (fawasil) a letter of the sort of the shapes': the divider is itself a letter-sign in the shape alphabet
فحلّه في الحال لسهولته = 'he solved it at once because of its ease'
plaintext_for: line 1 cipher: continues f. 82r block (plaintext lines 3-4 here); lines 7-10 block: plaintext line 11 on this page; a further cipher from line 13 heading continues overleaf
certainty: medium: crack at left of lines 11-13; names and several words uncertain. No dates, no AH years.

contents.direction_remark: NO dotted dividers at all in this block: a continuous string of Arabic-letter-like signs (ر, د, ه, م, ل shapes, one crossed-bar sign at top right). Lines 1-2 are strongly repetitive (a repeated 3-sign unit about 12 times, like a repeated word) and match the repeated 'kam' in the plaintext verse line 6. Line 3 is non-repetitive, line 4 is a short end. Not a continuation from the previous page (new item). Counts approximate.

contents.text: فحللته بعد صعوبة عظيمة وهو / فكم كم وكم كم وكم كم وكم كم وكم كم وكم يا ليل هذا / [التناسا؟/الثناسا؟]
contents.note: 'so I solved it after great difficulty, and it is:' then a verse built on repeated 'kam' (how many / how much), ending 'ya layl hadha' (O night, this ...); last word on line 7 not read with certainty ('al-tanasa'/'al-thanasa'?).

contents.text: واتفق أن أمين الدين المذكور كتب قصّة بأمر ما فرفع / المخدوم العلائي المشار إليه أسبغ الله ظلاله بما سأله وبعد / ذلك سأل المملوك نظير ذلك فرفع ببعض القصد وكان / معذورا ولم يسلم المملوك بالعذر إلا فيما بعد فكتبت له على / سبيل الانبساط وإدلال العبودية على إحسانه ومكارم أخلاقه
contents.note: 'and it happened that Amin al-Din the aforementioned wrote a petition (qissa) about a certain matter, and the master al-'Ala'i (?) referred to, may God extend his shadow, submitted it with what he asked; and after that the mamluk (the compiler) asked the like of that and he submitted (it) with some of the intention, and he was excused, and the mamluk did not accept the excuse until afterwards, so I wrote to him in the manner of familiarity and claiming the rights of servitude upon his kindness and the noble traits of his character'. 'العلائي' (al-'Ala'i) is read from clear letters but could be 'العلاني'.

contents.direction_remark: Letter-like signs with dotted dividers (about 6), a square-bracket sign at the left end; a crack/repair thread crosses lines 10-13 at right. Block runs to the foot of the page and continues overleaf (f. 83v). Counts approximate.

correspondents.note: no formula after his name on this page

FORMULA: 'asbagha Allah zilalahu' (may God extend his shadow) = alive when written. Whether he is the same 'makhdum mushar ilayhi' of f. 82v is not stated. Compiler calls himself 'al-mamluk' (the slave/servant).

technique_remarks: block with no dividers and strong repetition because the plaintext repeats 'kam' (how many)
فحللته بعد صعوبة عظيمة = 'I solved it after great difficulty' (the compiler solving, not a correspondent)
plaintext_for: lines 1-4 cipher: verse on lines 6-7 of this page; line 13 cipher continues overleaf
certainty: medium: names and several words uncertain; counts approximate. No dates, no AH years.

contents.direction_remark: Continues from f. 83r line 13 (the bottom line of previous page, same letter-like signs: ר/ד/מ/hook/square shapes with dotted dividers ~6 per line). Line 7 is short (about 7 signs) and ends the block; 'wa-mimma' follows at the left end of line 7. One or two stray small signs stand at the left margin of lines 1-2 (line-end overflow). Counts approximate.

contents.text: وممّا
contents.note: 'and of what' at left end of line 7, opening the next item

contents.text: يا ليتني أشبه المزّي [المرء؟] أمين الدين لمّا لحظته بعينك بالرضا / والله فداك ما سأله [?] في غاية التمكين إلى اليمن فلك قوي / [عزمي؟] وأمّا الصين [?]
contents.note: probably the plaintext for the cipher block (it is not introduced by 'fa-halaltuhu'). Reading very uncertain: line 8 may name 'al-Mizzi (the Mizzi) Amin al-Din' ('O would that I resembled al-Mizzi, Amin al-Din, when you looked at him with the eye of approval'); a small 'والله' sits above the line-9 start; line 10 is a short overflow written at the left under line 9, 'ʿzmy wa-amma al-Sin' (not read with certainty).

contents.text: وكتب له أيضا في ذلك إدلال المملوك الصادق المحبة على المالك
contents.note: 'and he also wrote to him in that [matter], the mamluk, true in affection, claiming rights upon the master (al-malik?)' (reading of the last word and the subject uncertain)

contents.direction_remark: New alphabet: Latin/Greek-capital-like signs (A, B, I, N, T, K, E, M, a lozenge, a hooked 'N') with dotted dividers ~4 per line; a paper crack crosses the left. Block continues overleaf (f. 84r) or is complete; counts approximate.

correspondents.note: plaintext line 8: 'al-Mizzi Amin al-Din' read from fairly clear letters but sense uncertain; no formula after the name on this page

technique_remarks: none stated on this page
plaintext_for: first block (f. 83r line 13 + lines 1-7 here): probably lines 8-10 of this page; block lines 12-13: no plaintext on this page
certainty: low to medium: plaintext lines 8-10 hard to read; no dates; no AH years; no rahimahu/ayyadahu formula.

contents.direction_remark: Continuation of the Latin/Greek-capital-like sign block that began at the foot of f. 83v (lines 12-13); same alphabet (A, B, I, N, T, K, M, E, lozenge, circle) with dotted dividers ~4 per line. Counts approximate.

contents.text: وأرسلته وهو / وكنت أظنّني بانتمائي إليك أنال ملء الراحتين / وما ذنبي سوى حبّي رضاكم فقلنا [لباس؟] لإحدى الراحتين
contents.note: 'and I sent it, and it is:' then two verse lines (uncertain words, esp. the end of line 7): 'I used to think that by my attachment to you I would receive the fill of both palms; and what is my fault except my love of your pleasure...'. Plaintext for the block lines 1-4 (and the block of f. 83v lines 12-13).

contents.text: ذكر الشيخ شهاب الدين أن المخدوم حصل له [إبراغ؟] وقال / رضانا يبغي أن لا يحصل له شيء قال فقلت له والله ما قصد / إلا الأجناس والصنعة والانبساط فقال صدقتَ وتبسّم / وكتبت له في ذلك حتى [أدلّه؟] بنشرح وعلم أن القصد الانبساط لا غير
contents.note: 'al-Shaykh Shihab al-Din mentioned that the master (makhdum) had [?] and said: [our pleasure wants nothing to come to him?]. He said: so I said to him: by God he intended nothing but the figures of speech (ajnas), the craftsmanship and the informal tone; he said: you are right, and smiled. And I wrote to him on that ... and he knew that the intent was familiarity (inbisat), nothing else.' Readings of lines 8-9 and 11 are uncertain.

contents.direction_remark: Another new sign set: boxes/squares with bars, H and double-bar shapes, small hooks (ل-like) and two-leg signs; a lone boxed sign and a small curl at the left margin beside line 12 (overflow sign). Dividers about 3 per line. Block continues overleaf (f. 84v). Counts approximate.

correspondents.note: no patronymic; no formula after the name on this page (neither rahimahu nor ayyadahu); he reports the master's remarks
probably the same 'makhdum' as in ff. 82v-83r; not stated

technique_remarks: القصد الانبساط لا غير = 'the intent was informality/familiarity, nothing else' (the cipher letters are sent in a playful spirit)
الأجناس والصنعة = 'paronomasia (ajnas) and artifice (sanʿa)'
plaintext_for: lines 1-4 block (and f. 83v lines 12-13): plaintext verses lines 6-7 of this page; lines 12-13 block: not on this page (next page)
certainty: medium: clear page; no worm holes; verse and report lines have uncertain words; counts approximate. No dates, no AH.

contents.direction_remark: Continues from the block at the foot of f. 84r (lines 12-13), same sign set: boxes/squares with bars, H, cup/hook signs, double-leg signs, and a triple-comb sign (three small combs) occurring at both the start and end of line 4. Dividers about 4-5 per line. A small stray sign (a tent/ground shape) at the left margin beside line 5, and a short Arabic word at the left end of line 6, apparently 'wa-huwa' (reading uncertain: 'ويد'/'وير'). Counts approximate.

contents.text: [وهو؟] / حلمك وجودك وبينك في النهى مشهور ومن بلد / بجنابك لم يزل منصور / [؟] تركت قلبي سيدي مكسور طلبت منك جميل / ما أعطيتني عصفور
contents.note: verse lines, in what looks like a colloquial/zajal-like register; probable plaintext for the block lines 1-6 (and f. 84r lines 12-13). Approx: 'your forbearance and generosity and ... are famous in intellect...; he who is at your side is ever victorious; you left my heart broken, my lord; I asked a kindness of you; you gave me not even a sparrow'. Several words uncertain.

contents.text: وكنت إذا دنوت من بابه العالي ترحّب بي علمانه تشير وجاههم / وتنكّرت ظنّا أن خاطر الكريم شغير ولم يكن كذلك / فترددت مرارا لم يؤذن لي بعد أن كان خبر وصولي
contents.note: narrative (the compiler about a patron, 'his exalted door', 'his boys/servants (ghilman?)'): 'and when I used to approach his exalted door his servants welcomed me...; and I held back, thinking the generous one's mind was (occupied?), but it was not so; so I went back and forth many times and was not admitted, after the news of my arrival had...' - continues overleaf. Words uncertain.

contents.text: [ومصدر؟]
contents.note: catchword at foot of page, left; reading uncertain

technique_remarks: none stated on this page
plaintext_for: cipher block lines 1-6 (with f. 84r lines 12-13): plaintext verse lines 7-10 on this page; the narrative lines 11-13 introduce the next item (continuing on f. 85r, not seen)
certainty: medium: page is clean (no worm holes); sign counts approximate; verse and narrative words partly uncertain. No dates, no AH year, no named persons, no rahimahu/ayyadahu formula on this page.
